## Journal articles

::: {.project-card}
[Published · 2024]{.status .status-published}

### Reduction of the shallow water system by an error aware POD-neural network method: Application to floodplain dynamics

**M. Allabou**, R. Bouclier, P.-A. Garambois and J. Monnier\
*Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering*, 428, 117094, 2024.

::: {.pub-summary}
A non-intrusive reduced model for 2D flood simulation: POD extracts a few
dominant flow patterns, and neural networks learn how they evolve, without
opening the simulation code. By accounting for the projection error, the
method stays accurate with few modes and small networks, even for
convection-dominated flows. Applied to the flooding of the Aude river
(southern France), it reproduces water levels and discharges of the full 2D
model and opens the way to real-time simulation of large floodplains.
:::

[Read the article](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cma.2024.117094){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}
[Related research](research.qmd#main-contributions){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}

## Submitted manuscripts

::: {.project-card}
[Submitted · 2026]{.status .status-submitted}

### Registering wetting fronts by dilation: a non-intrusive shallow-water reduced-order model with global mass closure for flood forecasting

**M. Allabou**\
Submitted to *Advances in Computational Mathematics*.

::: {.pub-summary}
Moving flood fronts are hard to capture with a fixed reduced basis. This
work maps the moving wetted area onto a fixed reference domain before
compression, and recovers the front position from the conservation of the
total water volume. The flow is then described with three to four times
fewer modes, and water-depth errors are 12 to 20 times lower than with
standard POD–NN. An ensemble of 10,000 flood events runs in about three
minutes on a laptop, making probabilistic flood forecasting affordable.
:::

[Related research](research.qmd#main-contributions){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
:::

## Manuscripts in preparation

::: {.project-card}
[In preparation · 2026]{.status .status-progress}

### Toward fast flood simulations via reduced-order 2D shallow water modeling

**M. Allabou**, L. Pujol, R. Bouclier, P.-A. Garambois and J. Monnier

::: {.pub-summary}
A reduced model of urban flooding, trained on high-fidelity 2D shallow-water
simulations over the city of Abidjan and tested on the real 2018 flood event.
It reproduces water depths and velocities over the whole event with
centimetre-level errors, and simulates the 8.3-hour flood in about 11 seconds,
roughly 420 times faster than the full model, a step toward real-time flood
forecasting and digital twins.
:::

[Related research](research.qmd#main-contributions){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
:::

::: {.project-card}
[In preparation · 2026]{.status .status-progress}

### Physics-guided regime-adaptive reduced-order modelling for shallow-water flows and flood uncertainty quantification

**M. Allabou**

::: {.pub-summary}
Instead of a single global model, this framework uses several local reduced
models, each adapted to a flow regime (wetting fronts, hydraulic jumps,
overbank flow), and a physics-guided classifier that selects the right one
during the simulation. On a 2D flood benchmark with 400 scenarios, it halves
the error of a global ROM, and it shows that reliable ROMs for nonlinear
flows depend as much on choosing the right local model as on the model itself.
:::

[Related research](research.qmd#main-contributions){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
:::

## PhD thesis

::: {.project-card}
[Defended · March 2026]{.status .status-published}

### Reduced-order modeling of the two-dimensional shallow-water equations using an error-aware POD–neural-network method: application to flood dynamics

**M. Allabou**\
PhD in Applied Mathematics, INSA Toulouse – Institut de Mathématiques de
Toulouse, 2026.

::: {.pub-summary}
A non-intrusive reduced model for 2D shallow-water flows, built from POD and
neural networks, with a key ingredient: learning the projection error, which
keeps the model accurate with few modes and compact networks. The thesis also
reduces the input signals (upstream hydrographs) with BiLSTM autoencoders,
forming a complete reduction chain from inputs to outputs. Tested on two real
2018 floods, the Aude river (France) and the city of Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire),
the surrogate predicts floods on large meshes in a few seconds, and points to
overflow-dominated urban flows as the next challenge.
:::

[About my PhD](about.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
